problem: A personal LinkedIn printer anecdote reappeared after earlier publication even though existing exact, normalized, shingle, source-fingerprint and keyword-overlap dedupe gates were present.
root_cause: The v2 semantic protection could miss a repeated concrete subject when the new wording shared too few total meaningful keywords and when source_text/content_id changed enough to produce a different story fingerprint. A single high-signal concrete object such as 'printer' was not itself a hard duplicate signal.
fix: Add cross-channel distinctive semantic anchor comparison to the canonical uniqueness reservation.
Block two shared distinctive anchors, or one shared anchor of at least seven characters, after excluding broad generic life/business domains.
Keep exact hash, normalized hash, shingle, source/story fingerprint and keyword-overlap checks cumulative.
Supersede personal source rotation that could recycle a used concrete story under a new angle.
prevention: Every social provider write must pass the global semantic subject/example uniqueness gate first.
The same concrete incident, anecdote, object-led example or story can never be republished on another date or channel by paraphrasing.
If no unused verified personal source exists, fail closed rather than inventing or recycling an event.

incident_example.allowed_future_behavior: choose a different verified personal subject/example

evidence.incident: On 2026-09-28 the user observed a personal LinkedIn post about a printer while an earlier printer post already existed.
evidence.existing_gates: v1/v2 already enforced exact hash, normalized hash, shingle similarity, source/story fingerprint and aggregate meaningful-keyword overlap.
evidence.observed_gap: A rewritten concrete anecdote can evade aggregate keyword thresholds when only one high-signal subject anchor remains shared.
